No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Team Nigeria Storm Liberia To Defend African Scrabble Crown by LEADERSHIP News 4 seconds ago in Sport Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram Team Nigeria have departed for Liberia to defend their continental title at the 16th Africa Scrabble Championship, which will feature 134 players from 24 countries in Monrovia.
The Nigerian contingent comprises 25 players who will compete against some of Africa’s best Scrabble players at the championship, scheduled to take place at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Ministerial Complex in Liberia’s capital.
According to a statement signed by Kola Daniel, Special Assistant on Media to the Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), on Wednesday, Nigeria will be seeking to retain its crown and maintain its position among Africa’s leading Scrabble nations.
Kenya have the largest contingent with 34 players, while Uganda are next with 30, reflecting the growing competitiveness of the game across the continent.
Nigeria, however, will draw confidence from its record of success in African Scrabble, having won multiple team and individual titles over the years and produced players who have excelled at continental and international levels.
The defending champions are expected to face stiff opposition from Kenya, Uganda and other participating countries, as increased investment, improved preparation and grassroots development continue to strengthen the sport across Africa.
The championship will also provide an opportunity for players to compete for individual honours while promoting Scrabble and strengthening sporting ties among participating nations.
For Nigeria, the immediate objective is to retain the title and sustain the country’s tradition of success in the sport.
The Nigerian players will rely on their experience, competitive pedigree and collective strength as they begin their campaign against a field expected to deliver a closely contested championship.
The 16th Africa Scrabble Championship is expected to showcase the continent’s growing pool of talent in a game that tests vocabulary, strategy, numerical ability and mental discipline.
